messages:
maria-chen: Quick question — a customer wants BYOK with an external HSM (Thales/YubiHSM/etc.) and they require monthly KEK rotation. How should we carve up RBAC for Redwood ops vs customer admins? Any audit/logging gotchas (proof of non-export) or legal concerns?

ajay-singh: High level: customer is key owner. Redwood must not be able to unwrap customer KEKs. Design = envelope encryption: customer KEK in their HSM, our DEKs wrapped with that KEK. RBAC: Redwood roles get wrap-only (or version_read) and never export/unwrapped plaintext.

leo_kwon: Also check retention — some finance/reg customers want >=7 years of audit logs. Make sure our audit pipeline can tag HSM-related events and retain per-customer SLA.

samir_garcia: KMS integration note: implement rewrap workflow. When customer rotates KEK, call their HSM to unwrap old DEK and wrap with new KEK, updating metadata. If HSM is remote, use short-lived session tokens + signed attestation.

maria-chen: If the customer's HSM is offline (network outage, vendor outage) how do we fallback without exposing plaintext?

ajay-singh: Two safe fallbacks: 1) approved legal/escrow break-glass (signed, multi-party, auditable) to rewrap DEKs; 2) route traffic to their private deployment where control plane is colocated and keys never leave their boundary. Both options MUST be logged with full chain-of-custody events.

maria-chen: I need a concise RBAC change request for Eng oncall (we'll need to update policies + terraform). Can someone sketch the minimal change?

leo_kwon: I'll draft. Points to include: - deny export/unwrap for Redwood service accounts - allow wrap & version_read for runtime agents - require customer-signed session tokens for wrap ops - emit audit events on wrap/unwrap with key_version and requestor fields

samir_garcia: Example policy snippet for the HSM gateway (pseudocode):
```
resource "hsm_key" "cust_ke" {
  allow: ["wrap","version_read"]
  deny: ["export","policy_change","unwrap"]
  audit: ["wrap","version_read"]
}
```

maria-chen: Vulnerability triage question: if vendor releases a CVE affecting the HSM wrapping primitive, what's our incident response? What's our customer notification cadence?

ajay-singh: Triage steps we should codify: 1) identify impacted HSM models/firmware and affected keys 2) determine exploitability (local vs remote) 3) notify customers within SLA windows (48h triage, 72h initial customer notice for high severity) 4) if exploit allows key compromise, immediately rotate KEKs and rewrap DEKs; if rotation impossible, trigger break-glass + isolate affected workloads 5) record everything in audit and run postmortem.

secbot: Incident runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hsm-byo-incident — includes notification templates and escalation matrix.

maria-chen: Good. Can we add tests: simulate rotation failure and HSM disconnect to ensure DEKs remain unreadable by Redwood?

leo_kwon: Yes — I'll add a unit test and a chaos test in our integration suite that simulates HSM unavailability and asserts DEKs remain encrypted and requests fail closed.

ajay-singh: I'll open a PR with the RBAC YAML + brief legal note for escrow wording. We should also add an enrollment checklist: attestation cert, allowed IPs, retention SLA.

maria-chen: Can security-ops validate the escrow wording and minimum audit retention requirements? @security-ops :eyes:

security-ops: Noted — we'll review escrow wording and confirm retention windows (SOC2/PCI/ISO cross-check). Will follow up in this thread with required language. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment 1773972000 to staging by ajay-singh succeeded :white_check_mark:

maria-chen: Thanks all. Closing loop — once PR and legal note are in I'll schedule a short runbook drill with eng-sre and security-ops.
